articleTitle: Development of computer-aided assessment for distribution protection
abstract: A simulation package for the assessment of overcurrent relay performance on interconnected distribution networks is developed which gives a new approach to identifying isolated nodes or split networks and fast detection of fault isolation in fault-current calculation. Other types of relay characteristics can be included into the package by simple modification of the program.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ageing characteristics of paper-insulated power cables
abstract: Most of the underground distribution cable in use in the United Kingdom is insulated by windings of paper tape which are impregnated with compounds of oil, wax and resin, in various proportions. The structure of this type of insulation is expected to deteriorate with time so that, even if the cable is mechanically undisturbed, the insulation may eventually be unable to withstand the applied electrical stress and the cable will fail. The author shows that under favourable circumstances a well-made cable may survive for several decades, but failures sometimes occur in cables only a few years old.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Managing an aging underground high-voltage cable network
abstract: The reliability of the UK high-voltage cable distribution network is most satisfactory, with the average failure rates around 2 faults/100 km/year. However, over half the network is greater than 25 years old, and a sizeable minority is greater than 40 years old. To manage this network economically and reliably, requires the ability to understand and measure the expected remaining life of the cables in the network. This is turn, means that the predominant long-term ageing mechanism, namely, partial-discharge erosion in the insulation, be quantified. Here, the author investigates which policy the power industry should adopt for the refurbishment and replacement of aged cables.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Special applications of power reactors in HV power systems
abstract: Power reactors find wide application in modern power systems. They have been used as shunt devices for reactive line compensation and voltage control; as series devices to limit short-circuit currents in busbars, cables and overhead lines; to reduce transient inrush currents that flow when large paralleled shunt capacitor banks are switched on; and as part of tuned filtering devices to reduce harmonic currents and voltages. The author examines some special applications of thyristor-controlled power reactors in HV power systems. He describes their principle of operation, the problems of harmonics and their suppression.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical apparatus for flammable atmospheres
abstract: The author describes in general terms the nature of explosive atmospheres, sources of ignition and electrical apparatus which can be safely used in explosion-hazardous areas. There are a number of different methods of designing electrical equipment to reduce the risk of ignition, each having a generic name such as flameproof, intrinsic safety, pressurisation etc.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Undergraduate teaching in electroheat
abstract: Despite the multi-disciplinary nature of electroheat, close scrutiny of the topics comprising it reveals the existence of unified themes which can be adapted with the view to teaching it as an undergraduate discipline. A case is presented, with raw statistical data, based on several years experience of teaching electroheat from its embryonic to a fully fledged stage as part of a third-year module.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systems approach combining traction, power supply and signalling
abstract: British Rail's Network SouthEast sector will shortly be introducing Britain's first fleet of trains fitted with induction motor drives. The author describes how optimisation of the benefits of these drives, and resolution of the potential problems that they present, has been achieved by consideration of trains and infrastructure as interdependent parts of an overall system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Construction, behaviour and application of electric fuses
abstract: Fuses were undoubtedly the first form of protection to be used in electric circuits, and they have continued to be used in increasing numbers up to the present day. Their importance can readily be seen from the world production of fuselinks, which is currently estimated to be several thousand million per annum. The author discusses basic fuse types and their construction. Fuselink behaviour, in particular arcing, is discussed. Applications of fuses are also briefly discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low smoke and fume type cables for BNFL Sellafield Works
abstract: Performance under fire conditions has been an important factor in cable design for many years. Indeed, mineral insulated cable which continues to be extensively used for many fire safety applications has been manufactured for over 60 years. The unique design which excludes organic materials was patented nearly a century ago and does not propagate fire nor produce smoke and fumes. However, fire safety is only one of many parameters to be considered when selecting a cable type. Here, the development of low smoke and fume (LSF) type cables and the factors which led to their use by BNFL are reviewed by the author.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sootblowing as a key part of powerstation efficiency
abstract: The author describes how sootblowing is used for in-service cleaning of the fireside surface of boiler tubes. The sootblowing system is one of the principal reasons for the high availability of power station boilers. Here, the author shows how the use of compressed air for sootblowing, rather than steam, can give added benefits to power-station efficiency in both economic and technical terms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The standby generation system at Sellafield
abstract: A 3.5 MW gas turbine generator has been added to the BNFL Sellafield standby generation system. The author describes the phases involved in taking a gas turbine from design stage through to installation and final commissioning. The author discusses the testing of the turbine and its operation, the commissioning of the gas turbine system and the problems encountered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Control and supervision of Sellafield electrical distribution system using a computer-based telecontrol system
abstract: Sellafield nuclear fuel reprocessing and associated waste management plant utilises 11 kV (HV) and 415 V (MV) systems in 55 substations to distribute a power demand of approximately 50 MW. Until 1985, the HV and MV distribution systems were controlled from a central control room using conventional discrepancy switches on a hard-wired mimic. During 1985, the hard-wired system was replaced with a computer-based telecontrol system to cope with the envisaged distribution system expansion due to the construction of major new plants. The telecontrol system controls approximately 245 HV and 360 MV circuit breakers. The author discusses the system requirements and the telecontrol system configuration. The operation of the system is described in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The impact of SF/sub 6/ upon power switchgear technology. I. SF/sub 6/ switch implications
abstract: A successful circuit breaker needs not only a suitable interrupter design but also a suitable medium in which to form and quench the arc. SF/sub 6/ is increasingly being used in circuit breakers as an alternative to oil and air. The author discusses the implications on switching technology of SF/sub 6/ use. The author discusses current interruption concepts and then discusses the distinctive properties of SF/sub 6/. These properties have promoted the evolution of new forms of interrupters which are described by the author. The performance capabilities of the SF/sub 6/ interrupters are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electricity-the flexible approach to industrial drying
abstract: The author describes the different types of industrial drying techniques, 'mechanical', convection, radiation and conduction. Examples are given of each type. The author discusses resistance heating, infra-red heating, heat pumps, an RF combination dryer, and a rotary induction dryer. The benefits of using electrical drying techniques are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spares strategies for transformers and transmission plant
abstract: The author outlines the spares strategies which have been adopted for generator transformers and transmission plant. Applications in respect to transmission transformers, switchgear and circuit and other substation equipment are described. The mutual advantages arising from sharing arrangements and co-operation on the basis of these strategies by the United Kingdom mainland generating boards is noted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical apparatus for flammable atmospheres: protection by flameproof enclosure
abstract: Flameproof enclosures are used in electrical apparatus so that, if gas enters and is ignited within the enclosure, the flame will not be able to ignite the external atmosphere. The enclosure must also be strong enough to withstand the force of an internal explosion without bursting, cracking or momentarily opening up any of the joints to an unsafe value.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of fuses to power networks
abstract: The first tutorial in this three-part series looked at the early use of fuses from 1864 and at basic fuselink behaviour. This second article considers the use of fuselinks in power networks including characteristics, I/sup 2/t values and operating frequency. A number of general matters are considered and then arrangements which have to be adopted to provide adequate protection and discrimination in a number of particular applications are considered in some detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sizewell B-the first of the UK's PWR power stations
abstract: The building of Britain's first PWR power station began in April 1987 at Sizewell. The project was subject to the closest public scrutiny on its design, safety and economical aspects. The 340-day Public Inquiry was the longest ever held in the UK. The author reports on a conference held in September 1989 which discussed progress to date. The design of the power station is discussed, and in particular the safety aspects. The equipment, and control and instrumentation are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cwm Dyli hydro station
abstract: Cwm Dyli hydroelectric power station is located in the Snowdonia National Park on the southern flank of the Snowdon range. The station was built in 1905 to supply electric power for the then prosperous slate industry. It is Britain's oldest power station, having been in almost continuous operation since it was first commissioned in 1906. In 1987, the station was shut down to allow for a complete refurbishment and uprating of its output from 5 MW to 10 MW. The author gives a short history of the station and describes briefly the 'new' station.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer-based control of London Underground's power network
abstract: London Underground now has some ten years' experience in the use of computer-based systems for the control of its power supply network. The initial application of computer technology, and ideas for future systems, all relate to the evolution of control methods from the early days of manned substations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Battery systems in nuclear process plant
abstract: Essential nuclear reprocessing plant process and monitoring systems require battery-backed supplies to ensure continuity of function during mains outages or disturbances. BNFL Engineering has provided many such systems to BNFL's Sellafield Site for both green-field site projects and refurbishment of existing facilities. The factors to be considered in engineering these systems are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development and implementation of a protection equipment test system
abstract: The State Energy Commission of Western Australia (SECWA) has co-developed a unique protection equipment test system (PETS) with a local Western Australian company called ACET Ltd. The test system uses an IBM AT compatible personal computer for direct operator control of 3-phase voltages and current sources. The author describes the development, method of operation and experience to date of the new equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Seismic implications for electrical services in a nuclear chemical plant
abstract: Earthquakes of any significance are rare in the UK. Nonetheless the nuclear industry is required to take this into account in the design of installations. BNFL Engineering has gained significant experience in qualifying equipment within the last decade.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IDMTL relay tripping of main incoming circuit breakers
abstract: Overcurrent and earth fault protection by means of inverse definite minimum time lag (IDMTL) relay tripping has been a standard solution for many years. In this case study the author examines the application of IDMTL relays for the tripping of LV main incoming circuit breakers as applied to installations in Hong Kong. The requirements imposed by the local supply companies and the consequent difficulties in achieving discrimination between the MICB protection and that on outgoing circuits are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of 11 kV power cabling on a nuclear chemical factory site
abstract: Continued load growth at the Sellafield nuclear chemical site caused a review of its high-voltage power system and its cabling. Type-test evidence was not available for the newer XPLE cabling systems. The authors describe how tests, in conjunction with the manufacturers, generated the necessary evidence for such a review.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rural electrification in the Third World
abstract: The importance of rural electrification (RE) in the development process is recognised in a number of studies and assessments of RE programmes that have been carried out during the past decade, by the developing countries as well as donors of foreign aid. The author reviews the RE experience of the developing countries, identifies the principal issues, and discusses how these problems might be resolved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hybrid UPS for standby power systems
abstract: Uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) form a major element in modern standby power systems. A wide range of UPSs with various designs are now available, and it is important to be aware of the relative merits of their electrical performance and how their operational characteristics reflect on the overall design and performance of standby systems. Optimising the standby system design is conditional on a complete 'system' approach being adopted. Various design aspects are discussed and a hybrid UPS scheme is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Overloading power transformers-a user's views
abstract: Users of power transformers often ask if the nameplate rating may be exceeded so that some exceptionally large load may be supplied. The cyclical nature of loads suggests that it may be possible to exploit the inherent delays in the thermal response of a transformer to changes in heating. Using accepted formulae and international standards, the authors shows that, in particular cases, loads exceeding rated values may be sustained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of 985 MW, two-pole, 3000 rev/min turbine generators for Daya Bay nuclear power station
abstract: Generators of 900 MW and above are required to match the unit outputs of the largest nuclear and fossil fired steam generators. Where steam and vacuum conditions permit, full speed, 3000 rev/min units are the most economic. In 1985 two 985 MW, 1158 MVA, 3000 rev/min generators were ordered from GEC Turbine Generators at Stafford for the Daya Bay nuclear power station in the Peoples Republic of China. The first of these generators is complete and has undergone factory tests before being shipped to site. The author discusses the design of the generators and gives a general description of them. The author then discusses in detail the stator and rotor design. The excitation systems, auxiliary systems and testing are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power distribution network design aided by an expert system
abstract: The next couple of years will see the need for replacement of a large amount of life-expired switchgear on the UK 11 kV distribution system. Latest technology and alternative equipment have made the choice of replacement a complex task. The authors present an expert system as an aid to the decision process for the design of the 11 kV power distribution network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experience with DC traction motors on British Rail
abstract: The author briefly discusses the conditions under which traction motors have to operate and then discusses their mounting on the locomotive. Cooling problems are also discussed. The various causes of failure and their repair, as well as routine maintenance are discussed. The effects of failure in service and the overhaul of traction motors are also discussed followed by details of faults specific to the various motor and locomotive types.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 150 kV Java-Madura submarine cable system interconnection
abstract: Because of the risk of anchor damage by ships using the busy port of Surabaya, Indonesia, the two 150 kV 120 MVA oil-filled submarine cables installed to link the island of Madura with mainland Java had to be buried up to 5 m deep in the seabed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rural electrification in Nepal: new techniques for affordable power
abstract: Deforestation and the consequent soil erosion are making daily life in Nepal even harder for the rural majority. Replacing wood with hydroelectricity as a fuel could help reverse this trend and provide scope for diversifying village economic activities, without further damaging the environment. Experience gained in Norway has been applied to building microhydro generators and to making the electricity they generate both economic and affordable. The author discusses these economic factors and then discusses the technical factors involved. This includes the generation equipment and generation control, the distribution network, house wiring, earthing of microhydro systems, metering, and end uses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Potential contribution of the energy-efficient house to system load-factor improvement
abstract: Habitational experience in an energy-efficient house confirms the potential for large-scale energy savings and supply load-factor improvement with a saving in overall building costs. This is achievable with 'run-of-the-mill' existing technology by: minimising heat loss through the building fabric; prevention of heat loss through draughts and air leakage, recovering the maximum practicable level of heat from the outgoing warm air; and using low-tariff off peak electricity for all space and hot-water heating.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
